question.problem:
Negate the following statement: 

$\,$ At least one prime number is even.
question.worked_solution:
Let $P$ be the set of all prime numbers. The given statement can be re-phrased as follows:

$\,$ There exists $p\in P$ such that $p$ is even.

Introducing the existential quantifier, we get the following:

$\,$ $∃p\in P,\,p\text{ is even}.$

Negating this, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(∃p\in P,\,p\text{ is even}) & ≡∀p\in P,\,¬(p\text{ is even}) \\  & ≡∀p\in P,\,p\text{ is odd}\end{aligned}
$$

which reads 

$\,$ For all $p\in P,$ $p$ is odd.

or simply

$\,$ Every prime number is odd.

choices.value: At least one prime number is even.
At least one prime number is odd.
